newsitem.title: USA: Latin American strategists urge bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Latin American strategists urge bargain-hunting.

text.p: Latin American equity strategists said Monday the recent drop in regional stock markets created buying opportunities at bargain prices.
Latin American markets, among the best performers in the world this year, have seen recent drops amid fears that Brazil could devalue its currency.
Here are some comments and picks from analysts and strategists:

-- "I believe the Brazilian market correction will be short-lived and the market will be higher by the next three-six months," Robert Pelosky, Latin American equities strategist at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, wrote in an analysis.
Among his stock picks are Brazilian telecommunications companies Telebras SA and Telesp SA, steel company Usina Siderurgica de Minas Gerais SA, or Usiminas, and bank Bradesco.

-- "While we recognize that volatility for Latin markets may linger for some time, we recommend accumulating the blue-chip companies in Mexico, Chile, Venezuela and Brazil," Bear Stearns Latin American equity strategist David Chon wrote.

His two themes for Mexico were "domestic demand recovery and market and market share gainers for top line growth." He said Venezuelan blue chips Electricidad de Caracas and CANTV "look interesting here."
Chon urged investors in Chile to "identify those companies which actively expanded their earnings base through investments and acquisitions during the past two years."
On Brazil, he added, "We would begin to accumulate positions."

-- Recommendations from Rehan Chaudhri, an international securities analyst at Brandywine Asset Management Inc in Wilmington, Del., included export-oriented companies. They were attractive since their revenues are in dollars and their costs in local currencies.
Among his picks were Argentine oil company YPF SA and Mexican glass company Vitro SA. Brazilian paper producers Klabin and Companhia Suzano de Papel e Celulose SA and Usiminas also were attractive.
"We've seen some real value emerging in Brazil," he said in a Reuter interview.
